newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 13.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 13.

text.p: -------------- GAM -------------------- REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
FRANKFURT - BBDO of Duesseldorf has bought the majority share of Hamburg media agency GFMO. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Streetad(d) Marketing of Coesfeld says it expects the support of cities and towns for its plan to place ads on manhole covers. It says a city the size of Frankfurt could expect income of about a million marks ($578,000), based on ads on 100,000 manhole covers. Each ad will cost a company between 400 and 1,000 marks. (Frankfurter Rundschau)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Germany's anti-trust watchdog has approved plans by media giant Bertelsmann AG and publishing house Axel Springer Verlag AG to set up a jointly-owned online sports channel, Bertelsmann says. The channel, called Sportkanal GmbH, is due to start within the next four months and will offer interactive sports information and programming on the Internet and for the German online service AOL, the joint venture of America Online,
Bertelsmann and Springer. (Reuter)

BONN - Telephone company Deutsche Telekom Ag says it will begin offering a video conferencing package based on computer chip maker Intel Corp.'s ProShare software. Business Video Conferencing, due to hit the German market in July, includes ProShare, which runs on personal computers, along with a new decoder for Telekom's T-Online service and a file transfer program for digital ISDN phone lines. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - Vehicle production fell five percent in May from the same month a year ago to 400,300 units, the VDA German automobile association says. After the decline last month, the number of cars made here so far this year was virtually unchanged from a year earlier at 2,131,500 the association
says. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Mannesmann AG says its group sales in the first five months of 1997 rose 16 percent to 14.3 billion marks ($8.3 billion), and that earnings in the period improved further. The automotive, telecommunications, and pipes and trading divisions contributed to the improvement, the company said in a statement distributed at its annual general meeting. (Reuter)
STUTTGART - Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG says that group

truck orders were up over 70 percent in the first five months of this year. Daimler, Germany's leading truck maker, also said it expected worldwide unit truck sales for the year as a whole to climb to around 400,000 units, what would be a 15 percent increase. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Franz Buderbach is now leading the new direct sales division of camera manufacturer Minolta's German division.
(Kress)
